takeaway: Renal cell carcinoma: the classical triad of haematuria, flank pain and a loin mass, seen in 10 to 15 per cent of patients.

question.text: A 45-year-old man has loin pain and haematuria, and a palpable mass in his loin. What is the likely diagnosis?
question.say: A forty-five-year-old man presents with loin pain and haematuria. He has a palpable mass in his loin. What is the likely diagnosis?

answer.say: The answer is renal cell carcinoma.

lines.text: Three little characters make the classic triad.
lines.say: Three little friends make the classic triad. Haematuria, flank pain, and a loin mass.

lines.text: Haematuria: red urine pours into the glass.
lines.say: The sick kidney pours red urine into a glass. That is haematuria.
The little kidney clutches its side. That is flank pain.

lines.text: And the loin mass: the tumour on the kidney.
lines.say: And on the big kidney, a tumour you can feel as a loin mass.

lines.text: Renal cell carcinoma is also called hypernephroma, Grawitz tumour or clear cell carcinoma.
lines.say: Renal cell carcinoma is also known as hypernephroma, Grawitz tumour, or clear cell carcinoma.

lines.text: The full triad occurs in only 10 to 15 per cent of patients.
lines.say: The complete triad is seen in only ten to fifteen per cent of patients.

lines.text: Remember: haematuria, flank pain and a loin mass mean renal cell carcinoma.
lines.say: Remember: haematuria, flank pain, and a loin mass mean renal cell carcinoma.
